title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a stratified space with strata X_i indexed by a poset I. The strata are assumed to satisfy the frontier condition, and each stratum has a tubular ('conical') neighbourhood V_i. For a flag (chain) d = (i_0 < ... < i_n), V_d denotes the 'standard' multiple tube, and V_{j,l} = V_j ∩ V_l. The previous page proved a lemma on pairs J, L ⊂ I with J ≺ L: J and L are bands (convex subsets), every element of J is below some element of L, and every element of L is above some element of J. Equivalently, inside the smallest band I' = {i : j ≤ i ≤ l for some j ∈ J, l ∈ L}, J is an ideal and L is a coideal.

This page applies the lemma. Put X' = X*_{I'}, the locally closed union of the strata in I', stratified by X'_i = X_i ∩ X^_{I'}. In X', X'_J is closed and X'_L is open. Formula (68) says that the 'generalized link neighbourhood' V_J^L := V_J ∩ X_L^* (a tube around the J-strata, cut down to the open part made of L-strata) is the analogous object computed intrinsically in X'.

The proof is as follows.
- V_J^L = (∪_{j∈J} V_j^{X'}) ∩ (∪_{l∈L} V_l^{X'}). The second union equals X_L^* because X_L^* is open in X'.
- So V_J^L = ∪_{j∈J, l∈L} V_{j,l}^{X'}.
- Case analysis of V_{j,l}: it is empty if j and l are incomparable (with a footnote that this needs connectedness or unibranch hypotheses). If j = l, it is V_j, and then j ∈ J ∩ L. If j < l, it is a standard double tube. If l < j, then because J is an ideal and L a coideal of I', both l and j lie in J ∩ L, so this case reduces to the previous one.
- Hence V_J^L = ∪_{j≤l, j∈J, l∈L} V_{j,l}^{X'}.

Grothendieck then wants to present V_J^L by gluing these pieces. He notes that V_{j,l} ∩ V_{j',l'} is empty unless {j, j', l, l'} is a flag. Such a flag has at most four distinct elements, all in J ∪ L, with at least one in J and at least one in L.

The next page completes this. The covering is indexed by the poset Drap_J^L(I) of flags i_0 < ... < i_n in J ∪ L with i_0 ∈ J and i_n ∈ L. This yields a Čech/descent spectral sequence H^p(Drap_J^L(I), d ↦ H^q(V_d, F)) ⇒ H^*(V_J^L, F).

Purpose: this is part of the 'déploiement' (unzipping) programme. The aim is to reconstruct a tame stratified space, and its relative links between groups of strata, from the system of tubes indexed by flags of the stratification poset.
errors: The emptiness of V_{j,l} for incomparable j, l is not automatic. It needs the frontier condition and suitably chosen tubes, which Grothendieck himself flags in the footnote (connected components, unibranch).
The equality ∪_{l∈L} V_l^{X'} = X_L^* presupposes that the tubes V_l^{X'} are taken inside the open set X'_L (tubes relative to X'). This is implicit rather than stated.
Minor point: only pairwise intersections are discussed here. Gluing via the flag-indexed cover also needs higher intersections to be the V_d for flags d, which is handled implicitly on the next page.

ideas.what: Relative link neighbourhood V_J^L = V_J ∩ X_L^* for a pair of poset subsets J ≺ L, computed inside the locally closed union of strata over the convex hull band I'
ideas.modern_name: generalized (homotopy) link between strata groups; link of a closed union of strata inside an open union; exit-path data between J and L
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988), Hughes (holinks); Lurie (HA Appendix A); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (links / unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches tame stratified structures and their dévissage into tubes; this specific J,L construction is not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Decomposition of V_J^L as a union of standard double tubes V_{j,l}, j ≤ l, with intersections nonempty only along flags; resulting cover indexed by flags starting in J and ending in L
ideas.modern_name: cover indexed by the subdivision (nerve/chain poset) of the stratification poset; unzipping / 'déploiement' of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzip), Lurie (exit-path ∞-category); Mather/Thom control data for the tube system
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 describes reconstructing a stratified space from a flag-indexed diagram of tubes, in outline only

ideas.what: Order-theoretic case analysis: l < j with j ∈ J, l ∈ L forces both into J ∩ L, because J is an ideal and L a coideal of the band I'

missed.claim: An explicit combinatorial model for the relative link V_J^L between an arbitrary pair of strata groups J ≺ L. It is given as a gluing of standard multi-tubes over the poset Drap_J^L(I) of flags beginning in J and ending in L, with an associated cohomology spectral sequence. Modern treatments mostly handle links of single strata, or exit paths between two strata. The 'interval' version for convex subposets, with this flag-poset indexing, is not commonly written down.
missed.quote: Pour écrire V_J^L par recollement des V^{X'}_{j,l}, il faut expliciter les V^{X'}_{j,l}∩V^{X'}_{j',l'} qui sont vides, sauf si {j,j',l,l'} est un drapeau.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a computable homotopy-colimit description of 'interval links' in exit-path ∞-categories and constructible sheaf theory. This is relevant to the AFT unzipping formalism and to recollement for constructible sheaves over convex subposets.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, technically correct working-out of the flag-indexed tube decomposition behind Grothendieck's déploiement programme. The overall idea is sketched in the Esquisse, and its modern counterparts (unzipping, exit paths, holinks) are well developed. The J ≺ L interval version is a modest unpublished detail rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: (68): the crossed word before 'de la forme' is illegible. 'voisinage' is a plausible reading, but the text reads 'le [?] de la forme V'_J^L, relatif à l'espace X'=X^*_{I'}, stratifié par les X'_i'.
Footnote in left margin: '* pour peu que les composantes des X_i soient connexes, X unibranche, ...' (approximately); it attaches to the case 'j,l non comparables'.

Left-margin NB reads approximately: 'NB pour cette formule, valable si J<L, donc on a (69) (signifie d'homotopie), on voit que V_J^L ⇒ V_J ∩ V_L = V_{J,L}', with V_J^L =déf V_J ∩ X_L^*. It is largely illegible and should be marked uncertain.
The displayed union carries index conditions j∈J, l∈L, j≤l under the ∪; there is no '[?]' after it, only a short horizontal stroke.
The word '[-?-]' in the struck passage near the end is likely '[-sont dans-]'; the corrected text reads 'au moins un dans J, au moins un dans L. Ce sont donc des drapeaux de la forme'.
